messages:
Maya: Heads-up — kicking off Q4 hosted API capacity planning. We have a converging set of signals: new EU customer onboarding + holiday-driven traffic spike + recent egress throttling in EU edges. I ran a quick baseline/peak calc and we need a hybrid buy/lease plan.
Maya: Numbers (A100-eq GPU hrs): baseline = 15,000/wk, projected peak = 20,250/wk (≈+35%) => delta ≈ 5,250 GPU-hrs/week.
Maya: Cost roughs: buy (amortized) ≈ $0.35/GPU-hr, reserved lease ≈ $0.80/GPU-hr, short-term rentals/spot ≈ $0.25/GPU-hr. Buying reduces long-term unit cost but 12–16 week lead time and creates regional imbalance.
Maya: Problem: EU egress throttles are shifting ~18% of EU traffic to US region for now (cache miss + cross-region fallback) — that increases US hotspot risk.
Ken: Procurement Q — if we decide to buy, what's the realistic calendar? 12–16 weeks start-to-ready? any way to accelerate?
Maya: Yes 12–16 wks for full rack procurement + install. We could accelerate with short-term colocation leases for 4–6 wks while hardware arrives. Also can stagger delivery (buy 50% now, 50% next quarter).
Liam: Quick question on model-side levers: if we push aggressive quantization + 2x shorter context on low-priority routes how much GPU-hr saving? ballpark?
Maya: From prior evals: quantization + kernel tweaks on conv models saved ~20–30% GPU-hrs for gen traffic, embeddings only ~5–10%. So we can target ~25% reduction for chat paths.
Sophia: I can run detailed sims this afternoon (per-route token distribution + quantized perf numbers). Pls drop the sheet link.
Maya: Sheet: https://docs.example.com/spreadsheets/d/abcd1234 — update tab "Q4-sims" with assumptions.
Maya: Example calc I used:
```
peak_tokens = 2.025e9  # tokens/week at projected peak
tokens_per_gpu_hr = 3.86e7  # empiric from A100 conv workload
gpu_hours_needed = peak_tokens / tokens_per_gpu_hr  # ≈ 5250
```
And then we split that delta across buys/leases/spots.
Andrei: Ops note — last warm-pool failover (staging 03/12) showed 150ms median latency bump and 3% transient 5xx on a subset of routes due to cache rehydration. We need to size warm pool for faster tail recovery.
Maya: Proposal: warm-pool = 12% of peak (was 10%), keep 40% of delta as buy (stable baseline), 40% reserved lease (predictable burst), 20% spot/short-term rentals for >60% spikes.
Ken: That split seems reasonable. What does cost look like over 12 months? Sophia?
Sophia: I'll run 12-month TCO + sensitivity (3 demand scenarios) and post by EOD.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary warm-pool-increase config applied to staging — smoke tests: ok :white_check_mark:
Liam: One more ask — can we add a routing rule to prefer EU-local cached results to avoid cross-region fallback when possible? even 5% less egress would help.
Maya: Agreed. Routing PR to route-team opened: https://git.internal/r/route/2345 — cc @route-team. If routing reduces cross-region fallback by 50% we can drop buy fraction by ~10%.
Andrei: Action items I captured: 1) Sophia runs TCO + sensitivity, 2) Procurement to validate 50% staggered delivery timeline, 3) Ken to validate colocation short-term quotes, 4) Routing team to prototype EU prefer-local rule and measure fallback delta.
Maya: OK — let's sync Thursday 9am PT after Sophia posts sims. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
